classical_condition: Unknown boundaries/background belong in event-recognition evaluation.
proposed_agent_mapping: Tool bursts, model waits and task intervals require an explicit observation unit and event errors.
reason: The open-world/unknown-boundary obligation still holds for Agents, but Agent execution adds tool bursts, model waits and task intervals that require an explicit observation unit and event-level errors before any event-recognition accuracy is meaningful.
notes: ANT-stage segments PCAP by session logs into primitive windows (li2026ant Sec. 3.2; 4.4) and never evaluates unknown boundaries/background traffic, so the classical condition is only partly carried over.

classical_condition: Evaluate adaptation to the protected distribution.
proposed_agent_mapping: An unchanged learner family can refit on protected captures; state training access and residual links.
reason: A defense claim against an Agent-side observer still requires an adversary trained or refit on the protected distribution; the mapped Agent papers must state training access and residual channels exactly as classical WF defense evaluation does.
notes: CG-transform/CG-live do run a defense-aware adversary (dangol Sec. 9.8; experiments/run_adaptive.py), whereas WRA-decoy/WRA-visibility keep the unprotected ICL exemplars (config_defence.json; utils_ICL_prompt.py:166) - i.e. the obligation applies as stated and is unevenly met.

classical_condition: Coarse features can survive specified padding; serving streams expose size/gap signals.
proposed_agent_mapping: Fix shaping policy, receiving hop, workload and feature protocol before transferring performance.
reason: The mapped Agent results compare feature subsets (e.g. CB-size-excluded drops size features) and traffic scopes on unprotected captures, but no specified padding policy, receiving hop or workload is fixed, so they do not test whether coarse features survive padding.
notes: CB-size-excluded (pouryousef Sec. V-B) drops size/byte features but applies no padding; ANT-model-scope (li Sec. 4.3) ablates traffic scope; neither fixes the shaping policy, receiving hop or workload on which the classical survival result depends.

classical_condition: Inference depends on visible paths and representations.
proposed_agent_mapping: Tool feedback can enter a later model request across separately controlled service boundaries.
reason: Visibility and representation still determine what is inferable, but Agent execution adds cross-boundary feedback: a tool result can re-enter a later model request at a separately controlled service, so the path and representation must be evaluated at each hop.
notes: WRA-prompt (jeong Sec. 3.1) sees only domain-level metadata; PT-metadata/PT-content (duan Sec. 3.2) see tool calls at a contacted service; ANT-model-scope and CB-task see encrypted packets. No single classical hop covers this cross-service feedback loop.

classical_condition: The STP implementation drops cover at its tunnel endpoints.
proposed_agent_mapping: Executed research cover needs original-task resource, state and feedback constraints.
reason: The need to check where cover is generated and dropped still applies, but Agent cover consists of executed research queries, so its original-task resource, state and feedback constraints must also be evaluated.
notes: WRA Sec. 8.1/8.2 do not report a tunnel-endpoint measurement; they measure leakage reduction and report utility (Table 11). Decoys are real executed queries, so cover generation is inside the task rather than at a tunnel boundary.

classical_condition: Distributed path reconstruction can use participating-host instrumentation.
proposed_agent_mapping: Instrumentation can label a study; it does not become a passive attacker input.
reason: Classical distributed path reconstruction assumes participating-host instrumentation, whereas the mapped Agent setting is a passive network observer; session logs can label a study but are not attacker-visible inputs.
notes: ANT-stage (li Sec. 3.2/4.4) uses PCAP segmented by session logs and AI-derived primitive labels, while li Sec. 1 states Agent communications are encrypted; a passive observer has no access to the host instrumentation that classical multi-host reconstruction assumes.
